rule.title: Boundary Request Validation via Zod Schemas
rule.statement: All incoming HTTP requests (body, query, params) must be validated by Zod schemas in middleware before touching controller logic.
rule.rationale: Unvalidated input is the root cause of injection attacks, data corruption, and unhandled runtime exceptions in downstream services.
rule.implementation_guidance: Attach a validate(schema) middleware to every Express route. Reject invalid requests with HTTP 422.

forbidden.example: Accessing req.body.documentTitle inside the controller without schema validation.

source.evidence_quote: Validation must occur at the boundary of the API. Any input that does not conform to the strict schema must be rejected immediately before processing.

rule.title: Strict Rejection of Unknown Request Fields
rule.statement: Validation schemas must strip or strictly reject unrecognized fields to prevent mass assignment vulnerabilities.
rule.rationale: Attackers can submit unexpected fields (e.g., isAdmin: true) that, if passed directly to database models, compromise security.
rule.implementation_guidance: Use zodSchema.strict() or ensure Prisma update payloads only use parsed, typed properties.

forbidden.example: await prisma.user.update({ where: { id }, data: req.body }); // Mass assignment vulnerability

source.evidence_quote: Mass assignment occurs when a client binds HTTP request parameters directly into data objects. Strict schemas must disallow unexpected properties.
